Query the Latest GHO Indicator Timestamp

Source: R/last_updated.R
gho_last_updated.Rd

Queries the latest non-missing timestamp among the current observations for one Global Health Observatory (GHO) indicator, without downloading its full observation table.

Usage 

gho_last_updated(indicator, backend = NULL, diagnostics = FALSE)

Arguments

indicator

A single, non-empty GHO indicator code.

backend

Optional WHO backend: "auto", "legacy" or "xmart". An explicit value overrides getOption("DSIR.who_backend") for this call only. When neither is set, the default is "auto", as in gho_data().

diagnostics

Logical; default FALSE. If TRUE, append diagnostic columns without making additional requests or changing backend selection.

Value

A one-row tibble with columns:

source

"gho".

backend

The selected "legacy" or "xmart" backend.

scope

"indicator".

indicator

The requested GHO code.

updated

The original timestamp as character, or NA_character_. Offsets, fractional seconds and an unspecified time zone are preserved.

timestamp_field

"Date" or "Sys_CommitDateUtc".

checked_at

The query start time as a UTC POSIXct value.

status

"ok", "not_available" (a successful response provides no timestamp), or "failed" (lookup, request, parsing or response validation failed). A missing timestamp does not establish that no observations exist. Failures warn and retain the same one-row schema.

With diagnostics = TRUE, six additional columns are appended:

reason

"timestamp_available", "directory_not_listed", "http_error" (an HTTP error response), "request_failed" (no HTTP response), "timestamp_field_missing", "timestamp_missing" (no non-missing timestamp returned), "unsupported_route", "lookup_failed", "unexpected_content" (HTML instead of JSON), "invalid_json", "invalid_response", "invalid_timestamp", or "fallback_incompatible". These explain status; they do not replace its existing three values.

stage

"directory", "availability" (automatic selection), "schema", or "timestamp": the stage associated with the result.

http_status

Integer HTTP status captured in that stage, or NA if unavailable, including a cached lookup or a transport failure. HTTP 200 alone does not establish a valid response.

timestamp_kind

"legacy_observation_date" or "xmart_system_commit"; neither guarantees an official revision date.

provider_route

The selected observation table path, when known. This contains no hostname, query string or credentials.

provider_indicator

The exact selected provider identifier: the legacy GHO code or xMart IND_ID, when known.

Details

This function is experimental. Availability and timestamp semantics differ between providers; the result is evidence about the selected API response, not proof of an official WHO data revision.

The legacy backend orders observations by Date; xMart uses Sys_CommitDateUtc in the same indicator route selected by gho_data(). Each date query requests only the latest non-missing value. xMart also consults the existing, session-cached indicator directory and table fields. Automatic selection follows gho_data(): a verified absent or completely empty xMart indicator can fall back to legacy, with a warning. Missing timestamps never trigger fallback. Explicit backends never switch. The who_provenance attribute records automatic selection and its reason; the backend column and timestamp field describe the actual provider.

The result describes the selected backend's current observations across all locations, years and dimensions. It is not the latest observation year, a formal publication date, or the update time of the whole GHO. In particular, an xMart system commit can reflect data processing. Backend timestamps need not describe the same release or event. DSIR has not established that legacy Date is an official modification or publication date. Several indicators can share the same system commit time without evidence that their published values changed together.

checked_at is when DSIR started this check, not a source modification time or data retrieval time. The latest observation year describes the period measured. Neither is substituted for a source timestamp. To detect actual differences between retrieved observations, use data_snapshot() and compare_snapshots().

A code absent from the public xMart directory can still be a valid legacy GHO code. A successful directory request does not establish that observation requests work. An HTTP failure does not establish that an indicator is absent. No indicator or backend is silently substituted.

See also

sdg_last_updated(), gho_indicators(), gho_data().

Examples 

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
gho_last_updated("WHS4_100")
gho_last_updated("WHS4_100", backend = "xmart")
gho_last_updated("WHS4_100", backend = "xmart", diagnostics = TRUE)

# Query several indicators sequentially using the same backend.
codes <- c("WHS4_100", "NCDMORT3070")
updates <- lapply(codes, gho_last_updated, backend = "legacy")
do.call(rbind, updates)
} # }
